correctness.rationale: With A=W⊕Z, Z=A^2 a one-dimensional annihilator, every subspace containing Z is closed, yielding a Gaussian coefficient. Subalgebras disjoint from Z are exactly graph lifts of zero-product subspaces S in U⊕V. The zero-product condition is orthogonality of the two projected subspaces; linear Goursat yields the stated a,b,t sum. The dimension cutoff d≤r and equality census follow. Direct RREF enumeration independently checks eight finite cases in CHECK.py, including characteristic two and the nonprime field F_4. Computations are only corroboration of the complete proof.

value.rationale: Determines an exact natural finite-field subalgebra dimension spectrum for an unbounded, canonically defined nilpotent associative family (the strict radical of three-block parabolics). The orthogonality/Goursat parameterization explains which subalgebras avoid the square and proves a structural sharp dimension cutoff and nontrivial maximal avoidance enumeration. Counts all dimensions and all q/r rather than a single ad hoc small-field table. This can be used in finite subalgebra-lattice investigations and differentiates associative closure from the familiar Heisenberg Lie analogue.
